action_history.rationale: Approach: Refine the size distribution by measuring each particle's true projected extent via boundary-based (Otsu foreground + distance-transform watershed) segmentation of the touching dark spheres, which sizes to the full sphere edge rather than the dark core and thereby corrects the LoG undersizing bias and internal-contrast fragmentation.

result.detailed_analysis: The analysis targets the size distribution of nominally 80 nm spherical Au nanoparticles imaged by TEM at a calibrated pixel size of 0.396 nm/px (810 nm field of view). The particles form a dense, closely-packed monolayer — dark-object coverage of 0.79 confirms the spheres are essentially touching, which is the expected physical regime for a drop-cast/self-assembled monolayer of monodisperse spheres and explains why blob-based (LoG) core detection plus a watershed fallback were needed to resolve individual cores. The interior size distribution (N_interior=93, edge particles correctly excluded) is tightly unimodal, centered at a mean of 68.8 nm and median of 69.6 nm with a standard deviation of 4.85 nm (~7% CV). This narrow, single-peaked distribution is the primary physical result: it indicates a monodisperse, well-controlled synthesis with no evidence of a distinct second size population. A small low-diameter tail (a handful of counts at 45-55 nm) most likely reflects minor over-segmentation / partial cores rather than a genuine sub-population, given its negligible weight and position well below the dominant mode. Critically, the reported median (69.609 nm) is IDENTICAL to the LoG blob median, meaning the headline sizes derive from the LoG intensity cores, NOT from the full projected sphere edge that the watershed step was intended to measure. LoG cores key on the dark central contrast and systematically undersize relative to the true projected diameter; the ~10 nm shortfall versus the 80 nm nominal spec is therefore consistent with an uncorrected core-vs-edge measurement bias rather than a real deviation of the particles from spec. The size distribution should thus be read as internally consistent and precise in relative terms (low spread), but with a likely systematic negative offset in absolute diameter.

scientific_claims.claim: The Au nanoparticle population is monodisperse with a tightly unimodal core-diameter distribution centered at median 69.6 nm (mean 68.8 nm, SD 4.85 nm, ~7% CV; N=93 interior particles), though these LoG-core diameters undersize the ~80 nm nominal projected size by ~10 nm due to an uncorrected core-vs-edge measurement bias.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: A narrow ~7% CV establishes high batch monodispersity, which governs the optical/plasmonic uniformity and self-assembly quality of the spheres; flagging the absolute-size offset prevents misreporting the particles as out-of-spec when the discrepancy is a measurement artifact, not a synthesis outcome.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone quantified the systematic diameter underestimate introduced by LoG-core (intensity-centroid) sizing versus boundary/edge-based sizing for densely packed spherical nanoparticles in TEM?

issues.location: Whole field — reported diameters vs. plan intent
issues.problem: The stated approach was to size to the FULL sphere edge via watershed on a filled Otsu mask, correcting the LoG undersizing. But the reported median (69.6 nm) is explicitly copied from the LoG blob diameter (log_blob_diameter_median_reported=69.609 == diameter_median), and the histogram/stats are the LoG core sizes, NOT the watershed region sizes. The watershed panel (n_regions=131) was computed but its equivalent_diameter distribution was never used for the headline statistic.

Green interior circles systematically undersize the visible dark spheres, sitting inside the true particle edge for many spheres. This is exactly the undersizing bias the plan set out to correct via boundary segmentation, but the reported size uses these undersized circles.
A minor population below ~55 nm (a few counts at 45-54 nm) exists; small but present, likely truncated/edge or slightly undersized detections.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Report the watershed regionprops equivalent_diameter distribution (border regions dropped, converted to nm) as the primary size result instead of the copied LoG blob median; keep the LoG count for N but decouple the reported diameters from it.
